rationale: ROUND 3 of trail bb7f5d0e. Two rounds of REVISE, and I am recording what each was right about because two of the three were my own sloppiness rather than design. ROUND 1 (bug_historian, HIGH): the fix was REPORT ONLY, and this estate has an owner ruling that a named log is not escalation (bugs_open/054), earned when bugs_open/018 shipped the observability half for dead controls and thirty shipped anyway. I had ANTICIPATED that objection and written the limit into the submission, the bug file and the code — and the seat's point is that stating a limit is not discharging it. Fixed by building the escalation. ROUND 2: I RESUBMITTED THE STALE SUBMISSION FILE — same path, un-updated contents — so the council graded the design I had just replaced. Entirely my error and it cost a round. ROUND 3 (editquality, HIGH): the arithmetic in my own summary did not close — 'nine of fifteen' while the enumeration listed seven, and 'six exceptions' while naming four. THE SEAT WAS RIGHT AND THE CAUSE IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX: my count came from `grep -c 'InputSchema = '`, which also matched `ci.InputSchema` in plan_sections_action.go — a DIFFERENT STRUCT with an identically-named field. A measurement that answered a neighbouring question, presented as a coverage claim. Recounted with a grep that names the receiver, and the true number was seven. I did not paper over the gap: I WIRED THE TWO MISSING PATHS, and they turned out to be the two that matter most — applyContentEdit and applyComponentSwap write rendered_html straight to an already-live page with no validate_content between, so a required field rendering empty there ships blank to a page that is currently serving. It is nine of fifteen now, enumerated both ways so the arithmetic closes. THE DEFECT, unchanged: Go's missingkey=zero renders a field the content never supplied as EMPTY WITH NO ERROR, page assembly drops the visually-empty section, and the content does not arrive broken — it does not arrive at all. That is the mechanism behind the fleet-wide blanking of article bodies (bugs_closed/004/005), and the gate that catches it ran at TWO of the fifteen render call sites. THE FIX is RFC_041 §5's candidate (a): the schema rides on the RenderContext and the SEAM applies missingRequiredLLMFields — the same function the two pre-render gates call, deliberately not a second implementation, so the seam and the pre-check cannot drift about what 'required' and 'empty' mean. It REUSES a dead slot rather than adding a field: SchemaSnapshot, SchemaMode and RenderOptions had zero readers since bugs_closed/260 deleted RenderTemplateWithValidation, so this removes three declarations describing a strict-mode validation the binary had stopped doing. THE GUARDIAN'S ALERTING QUESTION, CHECKED RATHER THAN ARGUED: no PrometheusRule exists in the namespace and no kustomize manifest consumes log level, so these Error lines feed no alerting surface outside this change's ownership. That is also the honest limit — nothing is watching, which is precisely why the work item matters more than the log line. AND A FINDING THE TESTS FORCED OUT: the seam and the pre-render gate give different answers on the same content and both are right — the seam judges the merged map the template sees, where contextToInterfaceMap defaults cta_text, and the gate judges the writer's output; 'did the WRITER supply it' and 'will it RENDER EMPTY' are different questions and 342 is the second. The seam's report is therefore a strict SUBSET. The first version of that test asserted equality, failed, and named the field.

plan.summary: ROUND 3, AS BUILT. THE ESCALATION IS IN THE CODE: the seam publishes which schema-required source:llm fields rendered EMPTY (ctx.AbsentRequiredFields) — it cannot escalate itself, having no database handle and no site identity — and the chrome path files a required_fields_missing work item, the type that ALREADY EXISTS for this defect with a router already seeded (bugs_open/277), opt-in with the unsafe default OFF. It reaches a population the existing producer is structurally blind to: check_required_fields_missing scans pc.build_status='deployed', and this defect's sections render empty, get dropped by assembly, and never become a deployed row. COVERAGE, RECOUNTED FROM THE CODE AFTER ROUND 2's ARITHMETIC OBJECTION WAS RIGHT AND MINE WAS WRONG: NINE of fifteen call sites now pass a schema — v3_site_actions (build), render_site_components (chrome store), rerender_page_sections, assemble_from_library, RenderHeader, RenderFooter, RenderHead, and BOTH section-editor routes (applyContentEdit and applyComponentSwap), which write rendered_html straight to an already-live page and which now ESCALATE as well as detect — round 5 was gated on my having called them the highest-exposure paths and then giving them a log line only. The SIX that do not: GateConvertedTemplate and tool_birth_instance_scope (raw candidate templates, no component), the legacy head render (loads a template only), RenderTemplateWithMap (a different executor, not this seam), and the offline audit's two calls (it probes with fields REMOVED on purpose, so a report there would fire on every probe by design). 9 + 6 = 15, and the count now comes from `grep -rn 'renderCtx.InputSchema = \|rc.InputSchema = '` rather than from a grep that also matched a DIFFERENT struct's identically-named field, which is exactly how I got 'nine' when the enumeration listed seven.

edits.rationale: The whole change. The seam is where all fifteen callers arrive, so it is where a guarantee can be made mechanical instead of left to each caller remembering — the same move as the existing form_action seeding and InstanceID report in this very function, and the reason candidate (a) beat candidate (b).

The escalation the gating objection asked for, at the one call site that has both a database handle and a site identity and already files two sibling item types. REUSES required_fields_missing rather than minting a fourth type: that type already exists for this defect and already has a router (bugs_open/277), so a new name here would leave the router blind to it. Also carries this file's schema wiring: it already parsed input_schema for the data-source fill, so the change is to lift that parsed map to function scope (the same reason `unresolved` is already at function scope here) and hand it to the render.
edits.sketch:
if recordAbsentRequired && len(renderCtx.AbsentRequiredFields) > 0 { emitAbsentRequiredFieldsItem(...) }, with the flag read from step config at the ONE caller (recordAbsentRequiredFields, default OFF, fail-open on a mistyped value) and passed in, because this function has no step config. The emitter mirrors emitChromeDeadControlItem exactly: shared insertWorkItem so it inherits the dedup and anti-churn behaviour, status `detected` and the same handler as the check so the same finding routes the same way, item_key required_fields_missing:<site>:<slot> matching the check's shape so the two producers co-dedup, and every failure logged rather than returned so the render never depends on the record being written.
SCHEMA WIRING, same file: `var parsedInputSchema map[string]interface{}` at function scope, assigned inside the existing parse block, then `renderCtx.InputSchema = parsedInputSchema` before the render. ⚠ Coverage note in the code: the FLAT chrome schema shape ({name:{...}}, e.g. 'Document Head') yields no field set from SchemaContentFields, so those slots are silent. Fail-open, stated where it happens.

plan.risks: 1) The escalation is wired at ONE call site (chrome). The build path already refuses pre-render so it needs none; the rerender path has a database handle and identity and is the obvious next candidate, deliberately not done in the same round. 2) Six of fifteen sites pass nil and report nothing — fail-open, tested, and recorded as residual in bugs_open/342 rather than a code comment. The offline audit is deliberately excluded: it probes with fields REMOVED on purpose. 3) The FLAT chrome schema shape yields no field set from SchemaContentFields, so those slots are silent; noted where it happens. 4) Item volume is unmeasurable before the fact for the same reason the defect is invisible — the population that would file items is exactly the population no stored row records. That is why the write is opt-in and why the first arming should watch the item count rather than assume it. 5) A new producer on an existing item_type means the router now receives items from two sources with different detection times; the key shape matches so they co-dedup, but a handler that assumed 'deployed row exists' would now meet an item where it does not. Stated because it is the one behavioural interaction outside this diff. 6) No migration, nothing armed on the estate by this commit, and the code is inert until the next chassis roll.
